- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.30) and forecast is rising, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment is positive (especially > 0.20) and forecast is falling, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to avoid underestimating rebound.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >2%), reduce subsequent 3–5 day forecasts by 0.8–1.2% to correct for overshoot.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 60–65), adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.0% per day until trend reverses.  
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is consistently negative and price is trending down, add 0.3–0.7% upward bias to avoid underestimating recovery.  
- If forecast is consistently higher than true for 3+ consecutive days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day to correct for lagged sentiment misalignment.
